newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia govt owes firms 76 trln roubles - minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia govt owes firms 76 trln roubles - minister.

text.p: The Russian government's unpaid bills to companies currently amount to 76 trillion roubles ($13.12 billion), First Deputy Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin said on Thursday.
He told a cabinet meeting regions owed a further 55 trillion roubles to companies.

"Now the federal government owes 76 trillion roubles to public companies and contractors which work by the state order and subjects of the federation owe their contractors for services and goods... a sum of 55 trillion roubles," he said.
He said the government would offer suggestions on how to settle the debts.
The Russian government is now stepping up efforts to repay its huge debts to people and companies.
Last month the state paid 22 trillion roubles in back pensions.

President Boris Yeltsin ordered the government to pay 7.7 trillion roubles in wages to public employees by the start of next year, including 5.2 trillion roubles in back wages to the military before September 1.
It was not clear whether the 76 trillion roubles included these wage arrears.

Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has ordered the government to settle mutual indebtedness between the state and oil and energy companies, First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko said.
The government is considering a possibility of securitising its debt, he added. ($ = 5,793 roubles)
